note: Item counts for the trolley photographs, established by looking at each one zoomed and at every numbered proposal drawn on it. Six of the ten photographs are one trolley being loaded, so the count is knowable at each step rather than only at the end, which is what makes this set worth more for counting than any other here.
product: one purchasable unit. Two egg cartons are two. A bag of apples is one. The trolley's own plastic disc is not a product, and neither is the shopper's tote bag.
rule: `correct` counts real products covered by at least one proposal. A proposal on a non-product does not subtract from it; it shows up as `proposed` exceeding `correct`.

counted.note: One item in an otherwise empty trolley. Two proposals: the cauliflower, and the white plastic disc moulded into the trolley's child seat. The disc is correctly detected and correctly not a product, which is the judgement `isProduct` exists for and which has never run.
One proposal for one product. The only exactly right photograph in the set.
Both found. The third proposal is the trolley's plastic disc again.
Three proposals, three products, one each. Exactly right.

Eight proposals. The tomatoes and the yellow bag drew nothing; both sit behind and under the purple bag. The baguette's box is loose, spanning it and the space around it, but it is the only box on the baguette so it counts as found.

The fullest trolley, and the only count here that is not certain: the shopper's woven tote lies across the middle and the purple and yellow produce bags are partly under it, so two of the sixteen are judged rather than read. Eleven proposals, one of them the tote itself, which is not a product.

not_countable.why: a produce shelf: dozens of punnets and boxes, most of them part-visible and stacked behind one another
the same shelf from further back
a meat cabinet, four shelves deep, packs overlapping throughout

non_products_note: Regions the census's `isProduct` field would reject, identified by looking at every numbered proposal. They are the whole of the over-count on this corpus. Recorded so the value of a step that has never executed can be stated as a number rather than asserted. At a lower detector threshold the shopper's shoes, visible through the trolley mesh, join them.
